saetze.kapitel: Chapter I. Into the Primitive
Chapter I. Into the Primitive
saetze.text: Buck did not read the newspapers, or he would have known that trouble was brewing, not alone for himself, but for every tide-water dog, strong of muscle and with warm, long hair, from Puget Sound to San Diego.

align.de: sonst hätte er gewusst, dass sich Unheil zusammenbraute,

align.de: nicht allein für ihn,

align.en: but for every tide-water dog,

align.de: mit starken Muskeln und warmem, langem Haar,

align.en: from Puget Sound to San Diego.
align.de: vom Puget Sound bis nach San Diego.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter I. Into the Primitive
saetze.text: Because men, groping in the Arctic darkness, had found a yellow metal, and because steamship and transportation companies were booming the find, thousands of men were rushing into the Northland.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter I. Into the Primitive
saetze.text: These men wanted dogs, and the dogs they wanted were heavy dogs, with strong muscles by which to toil, and furry coats to protect them from the frost.

align.en: These men wanted dogs,

saetze.kapitel: Chapter I. Into the Primitive
Chapter I. Into the Primitive
saetze.text: Buck lived at a big house in the sun-kissed Santa Clara Valley.

align.en: Buck lived at a big house

align.en: it was called.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter I. Into the Primitive
saetze.text: It stood back from the road, half hidden among the trees, through which glimpses could be caught of the wide cool veranda that ran around its four sides.

align.de: die an allen vier Seiten entlanglief.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter I. Into the Primitive
saetze.text: The house was approached by gravelled driveways which wound about through wide-spreading lawns and under the interlacing boughs of tall poplars.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter I. Into the Primitive

align.en: than at the front.
align.de: als auf der Vorderseite.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter I. Into the Primitive
saetze.text: There were great stables, where a dozen grooms and boys held forth, rows of vine-clad servants’ cottages, an endless and orderly array of outhouses, long grape arbors, green pastures, orchards, and berry patches.

align.de: in denen ein Dutzend Pferdeknechte und Jungen das Sagen hatten,

align.en: rows of vine-clad servants’ cottages,
align.de: Reihen von weinumrankten Dienstbotenhäuschen,

align.en: an endless and orderly array of outhouses,
align.de: eine endlose und ordentliche Zahl von Nebengebäuden,

align.de: lange Weinlauben,

align.de: grüne Weiden,

align.en: orchards,

saetze.kapitel: Chapter I. Into the Primitive

saetze.kapitel: Chapter I. Into the Primitive
Chapter I. Into the Primitive
saetze.text: And over this great demesne Buck ruled.

align.en: And over this great demesne
align.de: Und über diese große Domäne

align.en: Buck ruled.
align.de: herrschte Buck.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter I. Into the Primitive
saetze.text: Here he was born, and here he had lived the four years of his life.

align.en: Here he was born,
align.de: Hier war er geboren,

align.en: and here he had lived the four years of his life.
align.de: und hier hatte er die vier Jahre seines Lebens verbracht.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter I. Into the Primitive
saetze.text: It was true, there were other dogs.

align.en: It was true,
align.de: Es stimmte,

align.en: there were other dogs.
align.de: es gab andere Hunde.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter I. Into the Primitive
saetze.text: There could not but be other dogs on so vast a place, but they did not count.

align.en: There could not but be other dogs on so vast a place, but they did not count.
align.de: Es konnte nicht anders sein, als dass es auf einem so riesigen Anwesen andere Hunde gab, aber sie zählten nicht.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter I. Into the Primitive
saetze.text: They came and went, resided in the populous kennels, or lived obscurely in the recesses of the house after the fashion of Toots, the Japanese pug, or Ysabel, the Mexican hairless,—strange creatures that rarely put nose out of doors or set foot to ground.

align.en: They came and went, resided in the populous kennels, or lived obscurely in the recesses of the house after the fashion of Toots, the Japanese pug, or Ysabel, the Mexican hairless,—strange creatures that rarely put nose out of doors or set foot to ground.
align.de: Sie kamen und gingen, wohnten in den dichtbesetzten Zwingern oder lebten versteckt in den Winkeln des Hauses nach Art von Toots, dem japanischen Mops, oder Ysabel, dem mexikanischen Nackthund – seltsame Geschöpfe, die selten die Nase zur Tür hinaussteckten oder einen Fuß auf den Boden setzten.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter I. Into the Primitive
saetze.text: On the other hand, there were the fox terriers, a score of them at least, who yelped fearful promises at Toots and Ysabel looking out of the windows at them and protected by a legion of housemaids armed with brooms and mops.

align.en: On the other hand, there were the fox terriers, a score of them at least, who yelped fearful promises at Toots and Ysabel looking out of the windows at them and protected by a legion of housemaids armed with brooms and mops.
align.de: Auf der anderen Seite gab es die Foxterrier, mindestens zwanzig an der Zahl, die Toots und Ysabel, die aus den Fenstern schauten und von einer Legion mit Besen und Mopps bewaffneter Hausmädchen geschützt wurden, furchterregende Versprechungen zukläfften.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter I. Into the Primitive
Chapter I. Into the Primitive
saetze.text: But Buck was neither house-dog nor kennel-dog.

align.en: But Buck was neither house-dog nor kennel-dog.
align.de: Doch Buck war weder Haushund noch Zwingerhund.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter I. Into the Primitive
saetze.text: The whole realm was his.

align.en: The whole realm was his.
align.de: Das ganze Reich gehörte ihm.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter I. Into the Primitive
saetze.text: He plunged into the swimming tank or went hunting with the Judge’s sons; he escorted Mollie and Alice, the Judge’s daughters, on long twilight or early morning rambles; on wintry nights he lay at the Judge’s feet before the roaring library fire; he carried the Judge’s grandsons on his back, or rolled them in the grass, and guarded their footsteps through wild adventures down to the fountain in the stable yard, and even beyond, where the paddocks were, and the berry patches.

align.en: He plunged into the swimming tank or went hunting with the Judge’s sons; he escorted Mollie and Alice, the Judge’s daughters, on long twilight or early morning rambles; on wintry nights he lay at the Judge’s feet before the roaring library fire; he carried the Judge’s grandsons on his back, or rolled them in the grass, and guarded their footsteps through wild adventures down to the fountain in the stable yard, and even beyond, where the paddocks were, and the berry patches.
align.de: Er tauchte in das Schwimmbecken oder ging mit den Söhnen des Richters auf die Jagd; er begleitete Mollie und Alice, die Töchter des Richters, auf langen Spaziergängen in der Dämmerung oder am frühen Morgen; an Winterabenden lag er vor dem lodernden Kaminfeuer in der Bibliothek zu Füßen des Richters; er trug die Enkel des Richters auf seinem Rücken oder kullerte sie im Gras herum und bewachte ihre Schritte bei wilden Abenteuern hinunter zum Springbrunnen im Stallhof und sogar darüber hinaus, wo die Koppeln waren und die Beerenanpflanzungen.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter I. Into the Primitive
saetze.text: Among the terriers he stalked imperiously, and Toots and Ysabel he utterly ignored, for he was king,—king over all creeping, crawling, flying things of Judge Miller’s place, humans included.

align.en: Among the terriers he stalked imperiously, and Toots and Ysabel he utterly ignored, for he was king,—king over all creeping, crawling, flying things of Judge Miller’s place, humans included.
align.de: Unter den Terriern schritt er herrisch umher, und Toots und Ysabel ignorierte er völlig, denn er war König, – König über alles, was auf Richter Millers Besitz kroch, krabbelte und flog, die Menschen eingeschlossen.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter I. Into the Primitive
Chapter I. Into the Primitive
saetze.text: His father, Elmo, a huge St. Bernard, had been the Judge’s inseparable companion, and Buck bid fair to follow in the way of his father.

align.en: His father, Elmo, a huge St. Bernard, had been the Judge’s inseparable companion, and Buck bid fair to follow in the way of his father.
align.de: Sein Vater, Elmo, ein riesiger Bernhardiner, war des Richters unzertrennlicher Gefährte gewesen, und Buck versprach, in die Fußstapfen seines Vaters zu treten.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter I. Into the Primitive
saetze.text: He was not so large,—he weighed only one hundred and forty pounds,—for his mother, Shep, had been a Scotch shepherd dog.

align.en: He was not so large,—he weighed only one hundred and forty pounds,—for his mother, Shep, had been a Scotch shepherd dog.
align.de: Er war nicht so groß – er wog nur hundertvierzig Pfund –, denn seine Mutter, Shep, war ein schottischer Schäferhund gewesen.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter I. Into the Primitive
saetze.text: Nevertheless, one hundred and forty pounds, to which was added the dignity that comes of good living and universal respect, enabled him to carry himself in right royal fashion.

align.en: Nevertheless, one hundred and forty pounds, to which was added the dignity that comes of good living and universal respect, enabled him to carry himself in right royal fashion.
align.de: Nichtsdestoweniger ermöglichten ihm hundertvierzig Pfund, ergänzt um die Würde, die von gutem Leben und allgemeinem Respekt herrührt, sich auf recht königliche Art zu geben.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter I. Into the Primitive
saetze.text: During the four years since his puppyhood he had lived the life of a sated aristocrat; he had a fine pride in himself, was even a trifle egotistical, as country gentlemen sometimes become because of their insular situation.

align.en: During the four years since his puppyhood he had lived the life of a sated aristocrat; he had a fine pride in himself, was even a trifle egotistical, as country gentlemen sometimes become because of their insular situation.
align.de: Während der vier Jahre seit seiner Welpenzeit hatte er das Leben eines gesättigten Aristokraten geführt; er besaß einen gesunden Stolz auf sich selbst, war sogar ein wenig selbstgefällig, wie es Landedelleute zuweilen aufgrund ihrer abgeschiedenen Lage werden.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter I. Into the Primitive
saetze.text: But he had saved himself by not becoming a mere pampered house-dog.

align.en: But he had saved himself by not becoming a mere pampered house-dog.
align.de: Doch er hatte sich davor bewahrt, ein bloß verhätschelter Haushund zu werden.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter I. Into the Primitive
saetze.text: Hunting and kindred outdoor delights had kept down the fat and hardened his muscles; and to him, as to the cold-tubbing races, the love of water had been a tonic and a health preserver.

align.en: Hunting and kindred outdoor delights had kept down the fat and hardened his muscles; and to him, as to the cold-tubbing races, the love of water had been a tonic and a health preserver.
align.de: Jagd und ähnliche Freuden im Freien hatten das Fett niedrig gehalten und seine Muskeln gestählt; und ihm war, wie den kaltbadenden Völkern, die Liebe zum Wasser ein Stärkungsmittel und ein Bewahrer der Gesundheit gewesen.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter I. Into the Primitive
Chapter I. Into the Primitive
saetze.text: And this was the manner of dog Buck was in the fall of 1897, when the Klondike strike dragged men from all the world into the frozen North.

align.en: And this was the manner of dog Buck was in the fall of 1897, when the Klondike strike dragged men from all the world into the frozen North.
align.de: Und dies war die Art Hund, die Buck im Herbst 1897 war, als der Klondike-Goldfund Männer aus aller Welt in den gefrorenen Norden zog.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter I. Into the Primitive
saetze.text: But Buck did not read the newspapers, and he did not know that Manuel, one of the gardener’s helpers, was an undesirable acquaintance.

align.en: But Buck did not read the newspapers, and he did not know that Manuel, one of the gardener’s helpers, was an undesirable acquaintance.
align.de: Doch Buck las keine Zeitungen, und er wusste nicht, dass Manuel, einer der Gehilfen des Gärtners, eine unerwünschte Bekanntschaft war.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter I. Into the Primitive
saetze.text: Manuel had one besetting sin.

align.en: Manuel
align.de: Manuel

align.en: had one besetting sin.
align.de: hatte eine beharrliche Sünde.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter I. Into the Primitive
saetze.text: He loved to play Chinese lottery.

align.en: He loved to play Chinese lottery.
align.de: Er liebte es, chinesische Lotterie zu spielen.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter I. Into the Primitive
saetze.text: Also, in his gambling, he had one besetting weakness—faith in a system; and this made his damnation certain.

align.en: Also, in his gambling, he had one besetting weakness—faith in a system;
align.de: Auch hatte er beim Glücksspiel eine ihm eigene Schwäche – den Glauben an ein System;

align.en: and this made his damnation certain.
align.de: und dies machte seine Verdammnis gewiss.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter I. Into the Primitive
saetze.text: For to play a system requires money, while the wages of a gardener’s helper do not lap over the needs of a wife and numerous progeny.

align.en: For to play a system requires money,
align.de: Denn ein System zu spielen erfordert Geld,

align.en: while the wages of a gardener’s helper do not lap over the needs of a wife and numerous progeny.
align.de: während der Lohn eines Gärtnergehilfen nicht über die Bedürfnisse einer Frau und zahlreicher Nachkommenschaft hinausreicht.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter I. Into the Primitive
Chapter I. Into the Primitive
saetze.text: The Judge was at a meeting of the Raisin Growers’ Association, and the boys were busy organizing an athletic club, on the memorable night of Manuel’s treachery.

align.en: The Judge was at a meeting of the Raisin Growers’ Association,
align.de: Der Richter war auf einer Versammlung der Rosinenzüchter-Vereinigung,

align.en: and the boys were busy organizing an athletic club,
align.de: und die Jungen waren damit beschäftigt, einen Sportverein zu gründen,

align.en: on the memorable night of Manuel’s treachery.
align.de: in jener denkwürdigen Nacht von Manuels Verrat.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter I. Into the Primitive
saetze.text: No one saw him and Buck go off through the orchard on what Buck imagined was merely a stroll.

align.en: on what Buck imagined was merely a stroll.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter I. Into the Primitive
saetze.text: And with the exception of a solitary man, no one saw them arrive at the little flag station known as College Park.

align.en: And with the exception of a solitary man, no one saw them arrive at the little flag station known as College Park.
align.de: Und mit Ausnahme eines einzelnen Mannes sah niemand sie an der kleinen Bedarfshaltestelle ankommen, die als College Park bekannt war.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter I. Into the Primitive
saetze.text: This man talked with Manuel, and money chinked between them.

align.en: This man talked with Manuel,
align.de: Dieser Mann sprach mit Manuel,

align.en: and money chinked between them.
align.de: und Geld klirrte zwischen ihnen.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter I. Into the Primitive
Chapter I. Into the Primitive
saetze.text: “You might wrap up the goods before you deliver ’m,” the stranger said gruffly, and Manuel doubled a piece of stout rope around Buck’s neck under the collar.

align.en: “You might wrap up the goods before you deliver ’m,” the stranger said gruffly,
align.de: „Du könntest die Ware einwickeln, bevor du sie ablieferst“, sagte der Fremde barsch,

saetze.kapitel: Chapter I. Into the Primitive

align.en: “Twist it, an’ you’ll choke ’m plentee,” said Manuel,
align.de: „Verdreh’s, dann würgst’n ordentlich“, sagte Manuel,

saetze.kapitel: Chapter I. Into the Primitive
Chapter I. Into the Primitive
saetze.text: Buck had accepted the rope with quiet dignity.

align.en: Buck had accepted the rope with quiet dignity.
align.de: Buck hatte das Seil mit ruhiger Würde angenommen.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter I. Into the Primitive
saetze.text: To be sure, it was an unwonted performance: but he had learned to trust in men he knew, and to give them credit for a wisdom that outreached his own.

align.en: To be sure, it was an unwonted performance:
align.de: Allerdings war es ein ungewohntes Vorgehen:

align.en: but he had learned to trust in men he knew, and to give them credit for a wisdom that outreached his own.
align.de: doch er hatte gelernt, Männern zu vertrauen, die er kannte, und ihnen eine Weisheit zuzutrauen, die über seine eigene hinausreichte.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter I. Into the Primitive
saetze.text: But when the ends of the rope were placed in the stranger’s hands, he growled menacingly.

align.en: But when the ends of the rope were placed in the stranger’s hands,
align.de: Doch als die Enden des Seils in die Hände des Fremden gelegt wurden,

align.en: he growled menacingly.
align.de: knurrte er drohend.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter I. Into the Primitive
saetze.text: He had merely intimated his displeasure, in his pride believing that to intimate was to command.

align.en: He had merely intimated his displeasure, in his pride believing that to intimate was to command.
align.de: Er hatte lediglich sein Missfallen angedeutet, in seinem Stolz glaubend, dass Andeuten Befehlen sei.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter I. Into the Primitive
saetze.text: But to his surprise the rope tightened around his neck, shutting off his breath.

align.en: But to his surprise the rope tightened around his neck, shutting off his breath.
align.de: Doch zu seiner Überraschung zog sich das Seil um seinen Hals zusammen und schnürte ihm den Atem ab.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter I. Into the Primitive

saetze.text: It was all well enough in the Southland, under the law of love and fellowship, to respect private property and personal feelings; but in the Northland, under the law of club and fang, whoso took such things into account was a fool, and in so far as he observed them he would fail to prosper.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter VII. The Sounding of the Call
Chapter VII. The Sounding of the Call

saetze.kapitel: Chapter VII. The Sounding of the Call
saetze.text: They went across divides in summer blizzards, shivered under the midnight sun on naked mountains between the timber line and the eternal snows, dropped into summer valleys amid swarming gnats and flies, and in the shadows of glaciers picked strawberries and flowers as ripe and fair as any the Southland could boast.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter VII. The Sounding of the Call
saetze.text: In the fall of the year they penetrated a weird lake country, sad and silent, where wildfowl had been, but where then there was no life nor sign of life—only the blowing of chill winds, the forming of ice in sheltered places, and the melancholy rippling of waves on lonely beaches.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter VII. The Sounding of the Call
Chapter VII. The Sounding of the Call
saetze.text: He began to sleep out at night, staying away from camp for days at a time; and once he crossed the divide at the head of the creek and went down into the land of timber and streams.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter VII. The Sounding of the Call
saetze.text: There he wandered for a week, seeking vainly for fresh sign of the wild brother, killing his meat as he travelled and travelling with the long, easy lope that seems never to tire.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter VII. The Sounding of the Call
saetze.text: He fished for salmon in a broad stream that emptied somewhere into the sea, and by this stream he killed a large black bear, blinded by the mosquitoes while likewise fishing, and raging through the forest helpless and terrible.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter VII. The Sounding of the Call

saetze.kapitel: Chapter VII. The Sounding of the Call

saetze.kapitel: Chapter VII. The Sounding of the Call
saetze.text: But for the stray brown on his muzzle and above his eyes, and for the splash of white hair that ran midmost down his chest, he might well have been mistaken for a gigantic wolf, larger than the largest of the breed.

saetze.text: The years were not many when the Yeehats noted a change in the breed of timber wolves; for some were seen with splashes of brown on head and muzzle, and with a rift of white centring down the chest.

align.en: The years were not many when the Yeehats noted a change in the breed of timber wolves; for some were seen with splashes of brown on head and muzzle, and with a rift of white centring down the chest.
align.de: Es waren nicht viele Jahre vergangen, da bemerkten die Yeehats eine Veränderung im Schlag der Timberwölfe; denn man sah einige mit braunen Flecken an Kopf und Fang und mit einem weißen Streifen, der die Brustmitte hinablief.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter VII. The Sounding of the Call
saetze.text: But more remarkable than this, the Yeehats tell of a Ghost Dog that runs at the head of the pack.

align.en: But more remarkable than this, the Yeehats tell of a Ghost Dog that runs at the head of the pack.
align.de: Doch weit merkwürdiger als dies ist, dass die Yeehats von einem Geisterhund erzählen, der an der Spitze des Rudels läuft.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter VII. The Sounding of the Call
saetze.text: They are afraid of this Ghost Dog, for it has cunning greater than they, stealing from their camps in fierce winters, robbing their traps, slaying their dogs, and defying their bravest hunters.

align.en: They are afraid of this Ghost Dog, for it has cunning greater than they, stealing from their camps in fierce winters, robbing their traps, slaying their dogs, and defying their bravest hunters.
align.de: Sie fürchten diesen Geisterhund, denn er besitzt eine List, die größer ist als ihre; er bestiehlt ihre Lager in grimmen Wintern, plündert ihre Fallen, tötet ihre Hunde und trotzt ihren tapfersten Jägern.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter VII. The Sounding of the Call
Chapter VII. The Sounding of the Call
saetze.text: Nay, the tale grows worse.

align.en: Nay, the tale grows worse.
align.de: Doch nein, die Geschichte wird schlimmer.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter VII. The Sounding of the Call
saetze.text: Hunters there are who fail to return to the camp, and hunters there have been whom their tribesmen found with throats slashed cruelly open and with wolf prints about them in the snow greater than the prints of any wolf.

align.en: Hunters there are who fail to return to the camp, and hunters there have been whom their tribesmen found with throats slashed cruelly open and with wolf prints about them in the snow greater than the prints of any wolf.
align.de: Es gibt Jäger, die nicht ins Lager zurückkehren, und es hat Jäger gegeben, die ihre Stammesgenossen mit grausam aufgeschlitzten Kehlen fanden, und rings um sie im Schnee Wolfsspuren, größer als die Spuren irgendeines Wolfs.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter VII. The Sounding of the Call
saetze.text: Each fall, when the Yeehats follow the movement of the moose, there is a certain valley which they never enter.

align.en: Each fall, when the Yeehats follow the movement of the moose, there is a certain valley which they never enter.
align.de: In jedem Herbst, wenn die Yeehats den Wanderungen des Elchs folgen, gibt es ein bestimmtes Tal, das sie niemals betreten.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter VII. The Sounding of the Call
saetze.text: And women there are who become sad when the word goes over the fire of how the Evil Spirit came to select that valley for an abiding-place.

align.en: And women there are who become sad when the word goes over the fire of how the Evil Spirit came to select that valley for an abiding-place.
align.de: Und es gibt Frauen, die traurig werden, wenn beim Feuer das Wort die Runde macht, wie der böse Geist dieses Tal zu seinem Aufenthaltsort erkoren habe.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter VII. The Sounding of the Call
Chapter VII. The Sounding of the Call
saetze.text: In the summers there is one visitor, however, to that valley, of which the Yeehats do not know.

align.en: In the summers there is one visitor, however, to that valley, of which the Yeehats do not know.
align.de: In den Sommern erscheint jedoch ein Besucher in jenem Tal, von dem die Yeehats nichts wissen.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter VII. The Sounding of the Call
saetze.text: It is a great, gloriously coated wolf, like, and yet unlike, all other wolves.

align.en: It is a great, gloriously coated wolf,
align.de: Es ist ein großer, herrlich gefellter Wolf,

align.en: like, and yet unlike, all other wolves.
align.de: allen anderen Wölfen gleich und doch ungleich.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter VII. The Sounding of the Call
saetze.text: He crosses alone from the smiling timber land and comes down into an open space among the trees.

align.en: He crosses alone from the smiling timber land
align.de: Er kommt allein aus dem lachenden Waldland herüber

align.en: and comes down into an open space among the trees.
align.de: und steigt auf einen freien Platz zwischen den Bäumen hinab.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter VII. The Sounding of the Call
saetze.text: Here a yellow stream flows from rotted moose-hide sacks and sinks into the ground, with long grasses growing through it and vegetable mould overrunning it and hiding its yellow from the sun; and here he muses for a time, howling once, long and mournfully, ere he departs.

align.en: Here a yellow stream flows from rotted moose-hide sacks
align.de: Hier fließt ein gelbes Rinnsal aus verrotteten Elchhautsäcken

align.en: and sinks into the ground,
align.de: und sickert in den Boden,

align.en: with long grasses growing through it
align.de: durch das hohe Gräser wachsen,

align.en: and vegetable mould overrunning it and hiding its yellow from the sun;
align.de: das moderndes Pflanzenwerk überwuchert und sein Gelb vor der Sonne verbirgt;

align.en: and here he muses for a time, howling once, long and mournfully, ere he departs.
align.de: und hier sinnt er eine Weile und heult einmal, lang und klagend, bevor er weiterzieht.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter VII. The Sounding of the Call
Chapter VII. The Sounding of the Call
saetze.text: But he is not always alone.

align.en: But he is not always alone.
align.de: Doch er ist nicht immer allein.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter VII. The Sounding of the Call
saetze.text: When the long winter nights come on and the wolves follow their meat into the lower valleys, he may be seen running at the head of the pack through the pale moonlight or glimmering borealis, leaping gigantic above his fellows, his great throat a-bellow as he sings a song of the younger world, which is the song of the pack.

align.en: When the long winter nights come on
align.de: Wenn die langen Winternächte hereinbrechen

align.en: and the wolves follow their meat into the lower valleys,
align.de: und die Wölfe ihrer Beute in die tieferen Täler folgen,

align.en: he may be seen running at the head of the pack
align.de: kann man ihn an der Spitze des Rudels laufen sehen,

align.en: through the pale moonlight or glimmering borealis,
align.de: durch bleiches Mondlicht oder flimmerndes Nordlicht,

align.en: leaping gigantic above his fellows,
align.de: riesenhaft über seine Gefährten emporragend,

align.en: his great throat a-bellow
align.de: die mächtige Kehle dröhnend,

align.en: as he sings a song of the younger world, which is the song of the pack.
align.de: während er ein Lied der jüngeren Welt singt, das Lied des Rudels.
